questions.question: Where should carry-on bags be placed on a bus?

options.text: In front of the back door.
In front of the front door.
Where they do not block emergency exits.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where they do not block emergency exits.
questions.explanation: Bags must never block the aisles or doorways. All bags must be stored so passengers can exit through any door or window in an emergency.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat and makes a loud bang, when will the truck be affected?

options.text: Only if the flat tire is at the front.
Only if the truck is carrying cargo.

questions.explanation: There is a short delay between hearing the tire fail and feeling the truck affected by it. Because of this delay, the driver may think the sound came from another vehicle.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you before slowing down?

options.text: Tap your brakes lightly a few times before slowing down.
Wave your hand out the driver's window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes lightly a few times before slowing down.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights. This warns drivers behind you that you are about to slow down.

questions.question: How can you deal with blind spots while driving?

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so they cannot pass you.
Drive in the left lane so you only watch vehicles on your right.
Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to watch the traffic around you. This helps you notice if other vehicles are moving into your blind spots.

questions.question: If your load is too long during a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure all warning flags and lights are fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all warning flags and lights are fastened securely.
questions.explanation: If your load is oversize, check that all required signs, flags, lights, and reflectors are properly mounted. Make sure you have all required permits.

questions.question: What must buses never carry where passengers sit?
questions.explanation: Buses cannot carry labeled radioactive materials in the passenger area.

questions.question: If you are running late, what should you do?

options.text: Use flashing lights to make other drivers move out of your way.
Drive safely and arrive when you arrive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive safely and arrive when you arrive.
questions.explanation: Do not drive dangerously because you are late. Stay calm and accept delays. Plan extra time before your trip to reduce stress about being late.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel drowsy while driving?

options.text: Keep driving and try to finish the trip.
Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Sleep is the only effective way to fight drowsiness. Coffee and drugs may keep you awake briefly, but you will become even more tired when their effects wear off.

questions.question: To fix a drive-wheel braking skid, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Remove your foot from the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Turn the wheel back once the vehicle is straight.

questions.explanation: To fix a drive-wheel skid, first release the brake so the wheels can roll again. Steer quickly in the direction you want to go, then turn the wheel back to straighten the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the safest thing to do when you encounter fog?

options.text: Do not drive in the fog.
Follow the vehicle in front of you closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive in the fog.
questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see the road, other vehicles, and hazards. Avoid driving in fog whenever possible.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?

options.text: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread depth.
Rear tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread depth.
Use a gauge to check that each tire has safe tread depth.

questions.explanation: In winter, your tires need good tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Rear tires need at least 2/32 inch. Use a gauge to check the tread depth on all tires.

questions.question: With low beam headlights on, you can see about how far ahead?
questions.explanation: Low beam headlights let you see about 250 feet ahead. When driving at night, slow down so you can stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: What is a good rule when making a turn?

options.text: Use your arms to get other drivers' attention.
Turn off your signal before entering the turn to avoid confusing other drivers.

questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn so drivers behind you know what you plan to do. Keep your signal on during the entire turn. Turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: When can the emergency exit door be opened?

options.text: If the bus gets too hot while driving.
While the bus is driving if it is carrying cargo.
To get a better view while backing up.
Never while the bus is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never while the bus is moving.
questions.explanation: Check all emergency exits before driving the bus. Never drive with an emergency exit door or window open.

questions.question: Which is NOT a distracted person that drivers should watch for?

options.text: A driver talking to another person in the vehicle
Children on the side of the road
Construction workers on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Drivers talking with passengers may not pay full attention to the road. Children may run into the road without looking. Be careful around construction workers. A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus is not a distracted concern.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: Not enough oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A damaged exhaust system is dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not use the brakes. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This will slow the vehicle and help it regain traction.

questions.question: Buses must never carry:

options.text: Any amount of solid Class 6 poisons.

questions.explanation: Buses cannot carry tear gas, poison gas, liquid Class 6 poisons, or radioactive materials. Buses can carry small arms ammunition and emergency hospital supplies.

questions.question: When should you turn off your turn signal during a turn?

options.text: In the middle of the turn

questions.explanation: Signal early and keep your signal on during the entire turn or lane change. Turn off your signal once the turn or lane change is done.

questions.question: What can buses carry?

options.text: Explosives other than small arms ammunition.

questions.explanation: Buses can carry small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and drugs. Most other hazardous materials cannot be transported on buses.
